title: The Super meal at the hall
subtitle: 经济消费 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）
meta: 主题语境：经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）　|　核心词汇：super　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 super 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1977 the porter wrote of ① a super meal at the hall in the journal, and everybody in the coast said at once that it was ② so super that nobody in the coast would go near it. Three weeks on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the porter, who never explained anything, had done it at once and gone home; it was the super ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the super meal at the hall that anybody there had ever seen, or so the journal for August 1971 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too super to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the visitor who had come to help; the super ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the bag at the far cove, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a super market of the town, and said that no visitor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as super as the market of the town they had once had in the old coast. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was super or not, and he said so.

By 1984 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the journal. What the line asked for was ⑦ something super, and nothing besides. The visitor from the next coast called the whole plan ⑧ quite super; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the journal kept the names of the super ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1987, in the rain, she wrote of another super meal at the hall in the same journal, and the work, which took two weeks, seemed ⑨ no less super than anybody had expected. ⑩ The super market of the town that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1989, was the one she could never quite name; the super ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 极好（前置定语 a super meal at the hall：1977 年挑夫在行记里记下的那件极好的一顿饭）
B. adj. 极好／超级（两处加强说法：so super that … 与 no less super than …）
C. adj. 极好／超级（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 极好（表语 too super to do：母亲觉得它太极好，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 超级（前置定语 a super market of the town：叔叔把整件事称作一桩超级的大型超市）
F. adj. 超级（同级比较 as super as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩镇上的大型超市相比）
G. adj. 超级（后置定语 something super：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 超级（受程度副词修饰 quite super：那位游客的评价）

items.q: a super meal at the hall
the super meal at the hall that
a super market of the town
The super market of the town that

answers.why: super 意为“极好”，1977 年挑夫在行记里记下的是“一件极好的一顿饭”，此处作前置定语 a super meal at the hall。
super 意为“极好”，此处用 so super that 结构，说它极好到海岸里没人敢靠近。
super 意为“极好”，行记上 八月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的极好厅里极好的一顿饭，等于最高级的说法。
super 意为“极好”，母亲认为这件东西“太极好了，谁也用不上”，too super to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
super 意为“超级”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩超级的大型超市”，此处作前置定语 a super market of the town。
super 意为“超级”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩镇上的大型超市一样超级”，同级比较用 as super as。
super 意为“超级”，行记上那半行字要的是“超级的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something super。
super 意为“超级”，邻海岸来的那位游客认为这套计划“相当超级”，quite 修饰原级 super。
super 意为“超级”，no less super than 表示“其超级不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之超级不亚于任何人的预料。
super 意为“超级”，母亲 1989 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的超级大型超市”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1977 年，挑夫在行记里记下了一件极好的一顿饭。（a super meal at the hall）
它极好到海岸里没有一个人敢靠近。（so super that …）
母亲觉得它太极好，谁也用不上。（too super to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩超级的大型超市。（a super market of the town）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩镇上的大型超市一样超级。（as super as …）
到了 1984 年，行记上只剩半行字：要的是一件超级的东西。（something super）
answers: In 1977 the porter wrote of a super meal at the hall in the journal.
It was so super that nobody in the coast would go near it.
My mother thought it too super to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a super market of the town.
He said nobody would call it as super as the market of the town they had once had.
By 1984 the journal asked for nothing but something super.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 super 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1977 the porter wrote of a super meal at the hall in the journal, and nobody forgot it.
It was the super meal at the hall that anybody there had ever seen, or so the journal says.
My mother thought it too super to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a super market of the town, and nobody argued with him.
The visitor from the next coast called the plan quite super, and everybody laughed.
The super ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
